doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Charlie Parker tape and switching to stand-up bass
summary: She loved a Parker tape without knowing who it was, moved from electric to upright bass in sophomore year, and won her first solo award.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I didn’t know who it was and I found out later, like the first one I had and listened to over and over again was Charlie Parker, Bird, you know, with the tune “Laura” and the strings and all of that. And I thought it was great but I didn’t know it was Charlie Parker. And so I was listening to that and listening to a lot of other — I know he had a tape of Thelonious Monk, and then there was a tape of some Billy Taylor playing. So I got into listening to that and I was really intrigued by it, and at the same time I was starting to play jazz a little bit, and when I got to my sophomore year of high school I became more interested with the stand-up bass. First I had started on electric bass and then switched over to the stand-up bass because I saw it in a closet at the music school and I was like I want to play that. Nobody I knew played it. And so it was just from playing that I got more interested in jazz. And I did a competition in my sophomore year where I played, the first time I ever played a solo, and I received an award. I couldn’t believe it. So that helped fuel me to do more playing of jazz. And that’s really how I got into it.
